Simulate a Mach 2.0 compressible supersonic jet discharging into a larger 2D domain using OpenFOAM.
Use the density-based solver rhoCentralFoam as specified in system/controlDict.
Treat air as a perfect gas using hePsiThermo with equationOfState perfectGas and Sutherland transport (standard air coefficients: As 1.458e-06, Ts 273.15; Cp 1005, gamma implied by perfect gas with R 287.06).
Use laminar (viscous) treatment with no turbulence model.
Set nozzle inlet boundary conditions as fixed values: U = (686 0 0) m/s, T = 300 K, p = 101325 Pa (supersonic inflow at Mach 2.0).
Set far-field/outlet boundary conditions: waveTransmissive for p and T, zeroGradient for U.
Set ambient/far-field reference values p = 101325 Pa and T = 300 K, making the jet perfectly expanded (inlet static pressure equals ambient pressure).
Apply noSlip to all solid walls (viscous laminar treatment).
Use a 2D mesh with one cell extruded in the z-direction and the frontAndBack patch set to type empty.
Use typical geometry values: nozzle exit height 0.02 m, domain 0.5 m in x by 0.2 m in y, with the far-field boundaries sufficiently distant from the jet for shock structure development.
Choose reasonable mesh resolution sufficient to capture shock cells, with finer refinement near the nozzle exit and jet core.
Set endTime to 0.005 s to allow the shock cell structure and far-field to reach a developed state.
Use adjustable time stepping with maxCo of 0.5 or lower to maintain stability in the explicit density-based solver.
Initialize internal fields with ambient conditions (p = 101325 Pa, T = 300 K, U = (0 0 0) m/s).
Write results at regular intervals (e.g., writeInterval every 0.0005 s) for post-processing the shock structure.
